walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 2: Composing — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 2: Composing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 2: Composing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: It is the same as the chorus.
It has only five notes.
It is the very first section.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
It has only five notes.
Loud music with many instruments.
All notes are raised by a semitone.
It is the very first section.
A single melody with chord accompaniment.
Loud music with many instruments.
Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Note value”?
options: Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semibreve (whole note)”?
options: Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.

Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quaver (eighth note)”?
